messages.content: I want to buy apples, rice, and 12 pack of bottled water from a Walmart near San Jose. Show me the product information and stock availability.

function.name: walmart_purchase
function.description: Retrieve information of items from Walmart including stock availability. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

product_list.description: Items to be purchased listed in an array.

pack_size.description: Size of the product pack if applicable. The size of the array should be equal to product_list. Default is not use it if not specified.

message.reasoning:
The user wants product info and stock availability at Walmart near San José. We have a tool `walmart_purchase` which can retrieve item info and stock availability. It requires location (string) and product list (array). Optionally pack sizes.

We need to call this function with loc "San Jose" or maybe more specific like "Walmart - San Jose". Provide product_list ["apples", "rice", "bottled water"]? For bottled water we specify pack_size [12] because it's a 12-pack. So pass pack_size as [null?, but only one element]. Actually pack_size length equals product_list length; so provide pack_size [undefined, undefined, 12]? But default is not used if not specified. Maybe just omit pack_size entirely? But they ask specifically about 12 pack of bottled water. Might include pack_size [0,0,12], but better to set pack_size [1,1,12] meaning each other has no pack size requirement. Or simply supply pack_size [12] aligning with third item. Let's do:

{
    loc:"San Jose",
    product_list:["Apples","Rice","Bottled Water"],
    pack_size:[12]
}

But pack_size array length should match product_list length. If omitted, defaults apply. However we might still send pack_size [12] expecting first two ignored. Not sure how API handles mismatched lengths. Safer to skip pack_size altogether. But then can't indicate 12 pack. Could add separate field? No. We'll assume pack_size optional per item. Probably best to give pack_size [12] matching last item index? Hmm.

Let's check spec: "Size of the product pack if applicable. The size of the array should be equal to product_list." That means you must provide same length. So we could put nulls for others: [null,null,12].

Thus produce JSON accordingly.
